page: The Microsoft Azure E4bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine delivered via Microsoft Hyper-V on x86_64 architecture. Compute is driven by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache pool. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. The system is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high allocation of 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU. No local ephemeral storage or bundled GPUs are included, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Empirical benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-threaded execution. Single-core evaluations reveal a stress-ng score of 1894.78 and a Geekbench rating of 1639.0, both placing in the middle quartile. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including stress-ng at 3874.86, Geekbench at 3539.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 5855.46, position the instance in the lower tier due to its four-thread ceiling. Memory subsystem metrics reflect 208.44 GB/sec on small cached blocks, tapering to 29.36 GB/sec read and 25.78 GB/sec write on larger uncached buffers. Application tests report 3.81 million operations per second for Redis SET commands, 6.01 GB/sec in static web throughput, and 109.18 tokens per second on small model LLM text generation.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, the E4bs_v5 trades raw compute density for large memory capacity without incurring the expense of unneeded local SSDs. Relying strictly on remote managed block storage introduces dependency on external storage volumes, while CPU-intensive tasks such as parallel compilation and heavy decompression are bottlenecked by the limited core count. This resource profile offers practical cost efficiency for memory-centric, read-heavy workloads such as relational databases, distributed caching layers, and lightweight business applications that demand substantial RAM buffers without high processing concurrency.
description: The Microsoft Azure E4bs_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance includes 32.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio suitable for data-intensive processing. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA-NI. The E4bs_v5 does not include local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached block storage interfaces designed for enterprise systems. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest compute and multi-core throughput, alongside steady memory caching and encryption performance. Because the instance balances a high memory-to-core ratio without local storage overhead, it serves as a cost-efficient platform for memory-dependent tasks, including medium-scale in-memory caching, relational database hosting, and background enterprise application services.
